To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The quality of the teacher-student relationship, as well as the extent to which the teacher structures the classroom, are central to student motivation.

(1) the teacher-student relationship is important in motivating students; and (2) teachers can help students to be motivated by providing them with structure and autonomy support, which are the key ingredients in the recipe of motivation.
teacher behaviors that are related to student motivational outcomes (e.g., autonomy support) are also related to student engagement outcomes (e.g. behavioral engagement).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of teacher behavior in the motivational process.
the question of how to create and maintain a classroom climate that is motivating for students, and how to help teachers create such a climate.
the reciprocal effects of student motivation and teacher behavior.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
teachers' involvement in students' learning is the most important factor that can be controlled by the teacher to motivate students.
the teacher's role is crucial in the development of student engagement and that student engagement is crucial in the teacher-student relationship.
teachers should be involved, supportive and structured in their classrooms.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the student-teacher interaction is a dynamic, reciprocal process in which the teacher's and student's behaviors influence each other over time.

teachers who are more responsive to students and who create a classroom environment that is supportive of students' needs and interests, and that is structured in ways that help them to learn and grow, will have more highly engaged students.
teachers' interpersonal involvement is central to children's motivation in the classroom.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the student-teacher interaction is a critical context for understanding student motivation and engagement in the classroom.
the quality of the relationship between the teacher and student is a critical factor in motivating students to engage in the classroom and in their learning.
teachers' behaviors can be used to promote students' motivation and, in turn, students' motivation can influence teachers' behaviors.
